test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm on the principal axis of a concave lens with a focal length of 15 cm. Its image will be formed at a distance of □( ).
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image of the object placed in front of it.
 
• The lens formula for a concave lens is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u** where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• Given the focal length (f) is -15 cm (negative for concave lens) and the object distance (u) is -30 cm (negative as per sign convention).
 
• Using the lens formula, 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/(-15) + 1/(-30) = -1/15 - 1/30 = -2/30 - 1/30 = -3/30 = -1/10, thus v = -10 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Lens:**

 
 
• A concave lens, also known as a diverging lens, is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It causes parallel rays of light to diverge after passing through it.
 
• The focal length of a concave lens is negative.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• The lens formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a lens.
 
• It is given by the equation 1/f = 1/v - 1/u.
 
• This formula is applicable to both concave and convex lenses.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• In the sign convention for lenses, distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive, and those measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
 
• For concave lenses, the focal length is always negative.
 
• The object distance (u) is negative if the object is placed on the same side as the incident light.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Lens:**
 
 
• A concave lens always forms a virtual image, which means the image cannot be projected on a screen.
 
• The image formed is always erect and smaller than the object.
 
• The image distance (v) for a concave lens is always negative, indicating that the image is formed on the same side as the object.
